subject: English
topic: Reading Comprehension II — inference, tone, title, vocabulary in context
description: RC skills: identifying main idea, author tone, inference questions, vocabulary in context, title selection, fact vs inference distinction.

questions.stem: In an RC passage the author states: 'While renewable energy has made remarkable progress, dismissing fossil fuels overnight would be naive.' The author's tone is best described as:

options.option_text: Balanced/pragmatic — acknowledges renewables' progress while cautioning against hasty fossil fuel elimination
Strongly pro-fossil fuel — the author defends fossil fuels and attacks renewable energy
Pessimistic about renewables — the author doubts renewables can ever replace fossil fuels
Sarcastic — the tone is measured and rational, not satirical or mocking (not this) instead

questions.explanation: TONE ANALYSIS: 'remarkable progress' = positive view of renewables. 'would be naive' = caution against rushing. The author is NOT anti-renewable (uses 'remarkable') nor anti-fossil (says dismissal would be naive). This is a balanced, pragmatic stance. EXAM SKILL: identify what the author affirms vs qualifies. Balanced tone = acknowledges both sides. Other tones: cynical (general distrust), optimistic (unconditional positivity), alarmist (urgent fear). PYQ: tone questions are the most commonly tested RC skill in IBPS PO/Clerk English.

questions.stem: A passage discusses how social media algorithms amplify outrage to maximise engagement, leading to polarisation. Which title best captures the central idea?

options.option_text: Outrage as a Business Model: How Algorithms Profit from Division — directly captures the engagement-outrage-polarisation link
The Benefits of Social Media for Modern Communication — ignores the critical, negative focus of the passage
History of Social Media Platforms from 2004 to Present — the passage is thematic, not historical/chronological
How to Reduce Your Screen Time Effectively — the passage is analytical, not prescriptive self-help advice

questions.explanation: TITLE SELECTION SKILL: the best title must capture the CENTRAL ARGUMENT, not a peripheral detail or misrepresent the tone. Key elements of this passage: algorithms, outrage amplification, engagement motive (business model), polarisation result. Option A captures all four elements. Option B is opposite in tone. Option C is off-topic (historical). Option D is practical self-help — irrelevant to the analytical argument. EXAM RULE: the correct title for analytical/argumentative passages almost always mirrors the cause-effect chain at the core of the argument.

questions.stem: A passage states: 'Despite India's significant strides in digital infrastructure, rural areas remain largely excluded from the benefits.' Which inference is MOST valid?

options.option_text: Digital inclusion in India is uneven, with a persistent rural-urban digital divide
India has no digital infrastructure at all — the word 'significant strides' contradicts this conclusion
Rural areas prefer to remain offline by choice rather than due to infrastructure gaps
Digital infrastructure is more advanced in India than in any other developing nation

questions.explanation: INFERENCE SKILL: valid inference = conclusion that logically follows from what the passage states, without going beyond it. PASSAGE SAYS: (1) India has made significant digital progress. (2) Rural areas remain excluded. INFERENCE A: 'uneven digital inclusion / rural-urban divide' — directly supported by both elements. INVALID INFERENCES: B contradicts 'significant strides.' C introduces an unsupported claim about preference. D introduces a comparative global claim not mentioned. EXAM RULE: the correct inference never contradicts the passage and never introduces outside information — it is the logical conclusion of what is explicitly stated.

questions.stem: In a passage, the word 'INIMICAL' appears in the sentence: 'Such policies are inimical to long-term economic growth.' In this context, 'inimical' most nearly means:

options.option_text: Harmful or hostile to — inimical (from Latin inimicus = enemy) means actively adverse or damaging to
Beneficial to — opposite meaning; 'inimical to growth' means damaging, not helping growth
Neutral toward — inimical is not neutral; it implies active opposition or harm
Unrelated to — the sentence implies a direct negative relationship, not irrelevance

questions.explanation: INIMICAL: from Latin INIMICUS (enemy). Means: HARMFUL TO, HOSTILE TO, ADVERSE TO. 'Inimical to growth' = harmful to growth/working against growth. FAMILY: enemy, enmity, inimical — all from the same root. USAGE: 'practices inimical to public health'; 'conditions inimical to democracy.' CONTEXT CLUE: the sentence criticises the policies (they harm something long-term) — this narrows the meaning to 'harmful/hostile.' PYQ: 'inimical' appears in IBPS PO RC passages; vocabulary-in-context questions require using the sentence context, not just memorised definitions.

questions.stem: A passage argues: 'Microfinance has empowered women in rural India by giving them financial agency, yet it has also burdened some with unmanageable debt cycles.' The author's primary purpose is to:

options.option_text: Present a nuanced assessment — acknowledging microfinance's empowerment potential while flagging its debt-trap risk
Advocate for abolishing microfinance — a blanket rejection is not supported; the author acknowledges the benefits too
Promote microfinance as a solution for rural poverty without qualification — this ignores the second half of the statement
Compare Indian microfinance with international models — no comparison with other countries is present in the passage

questions.explanation: PURPOSE IDENTIFICATION: look at what the author is trying to DO with the text. The sentence has TWO parts connected by 'yet': (1) positive = financial agency/empowerment. (2) negative = debt burden. The author's purpose is to give a BALANCED/NUANCED view — neither wholly endorsing nor condemning microfinance. EXAM SKILL: when a passage uses 'yet,' 'however,' 'but,' 'despite' — the author is making a two-sided argument. The purpose is assessment/evaluation, not advocacy or comparison. PYQ: author's purpose questions are tested in every IBPS PO mains English section.

questions.stem: In an RC passage about urban planning: 'The city's arterial roads, designed in the 1970s, are now choked by a volume of traffic that was inconceivable to their planners.' What does 'arterial' most likely mean in this context?

options.option_text: Main or principal — arterial roads are the main routes, like arteries carrying blood in the body
Medical or surgical — 'arterial' here is a metaphor, not a reference to human anatomy
Ancient or historical — arterial refers to function (main route), not age of the road
Narrow and congested — the congestion is caused by traffic volume, not the road's original design width

questions.explanation: ARTERIAL (roads): from ARTERY (blood vessel carrying blood from heart). Metaphorical extension: arterial road = a major road that carries the main flow of traffic, like an artery carries blood. CONTEXT CLUES: 'choked by a volume of traffic' confirms these roads are meant to carry large traffic flows (= main roads). 'Designed in the 1970s' refers to their history, not their definition. URBAN PLANNING VOCABULARY: arterial (main), collector (secondary), local (residential). PYQ: vocabulary in context from urban planning/economics passages appears in IBPS PO mains RC.

questions.stem: A passage concludes: 'It is not the absence of talent but the absence of systems that perpetuates poverty.' Which of the following best identifies the author's implied assumption?

options.option_text: Talent is evenly distributed; poverty persists because institutional and systemic support is lacking
Poor people lack the talent to escape poverty regardless of external support systems
Systems alone cannot address poverty; individual talent must also be cultivated deliberately
The author believes poverty is primarily a cultural phenomenon linked to values and attitudes

questions.explanation: IMPLIED ASSUMPTION: the unstated premise that makes the argument logically valid. The author's argument: poverty is NOT due to lack of talent; it IS due to lack of systems. ASSUMPTION required: talent is present (distributed) — otherwise saying 'absence of systems' is the cause would be incomplete. The statement implies: talent exists everywhere but systems (education, credit, infrastructure, opportunity) are absent for the poor. STRUCTURAL ARGUMENT: this is a classic 'not X but Y' construction — the assumption is that X (talent) is NOT the problem. PYQ: implied assumption questions appear in IBPS PO mains critical reasoning / RC sections.

questions.stem: A passage reads: 'The handloom sector, often romanticised in policy speeches, continues to struggle under synthetic substitutes and inadequate market linkages. Weavers who once took pride in their craft are now compelled to seek daily-wage labour in urban centres.' What is the dominant tone of this passage?

options.option_text: Celebratory and optimistic about handloom sector revival
Critical and concerned about the handloom sector's ongoing decline
Neutral and purely descriptive of weaver community practices
Satirical and dismissive of all government policy on crafts

questions.explanation: B is correct because words like 'romanticised' (implying false praise), 'continues to struggle', and 'compelled to seek daily-wage labour' signal a critical, concerned stance about the sector's decline. Option A is wrong because the passage explicitly highlights failures, not successes; there is no optimism here.

questions.stem: A passage states: 'Mangrove forests buffer coastlines against cyclones, sequester carbon at rates exceeding terrestrial forests, and provide marine nursery habitats. Yet India loses thousands of hectares of mangroves annually to shrimp farming and coastal construction projects.' Which title best captures the central idea?

options.option_text: Shrimp Farming: A Rising Threat to India's Coastal Economy
Mangroves: Ecologically Vital Forests Facing Rapid Destruction
Carbon Sequestration Strategies in India's Coastal Wetlands
Marine Biodiversity and the Importance of Nursery Habitats

questions.explanation: B is correct because the passage covers multiple ecological roles of mangroves AND their destruction — both elements must appear in the title. Option C is wrong because carbon sequestration is only one point among several; the passage is not focused exclusively on climate science.

questions.stem: A passage reads: 'The 73rd Constitutional Amendment empowered Panchayati Raj Institutions on paper, yet gram sabhas rarely convene, women representatives are frequently proxies for male relatives, and devolved funds are regularly diverted.' What can be reasonably inferred from this passage?

options.option_text: The 73rd Amendment was largely redundant for rural governance reform altogether
Formal legal empowerment does not automatically guarantee effective decentralisation
Women representatives should be phased out of Panchayati Raj Institutions entirely
Gram sabhas are the single weakest institution in India's entire federal structure

questions.explanation: B is correct because the passage contrasts what exists 'on paper' with what happens in practice — this gap directly illustrates that legislation alone is insufficient. Option A is wrong because the author does not say the Amendment was unnecessary; the critique is about implementation failure, not the law's intent.

questions.stem: A passage reads: 'The committee's report on the dam project was deliberately equivocal, neither endorsing the environmental clearance nor rejecting it outright, leaving bureaucrats free to interpret it as they wished.' In this context, 'EQUIVOCAL' most nearly means?

options.option_text: Strongly worded and free of any ambiguity in its recommendations
Intentionally vague and open to more than one interpretation
Technically precise but challenging for laypeople to comprehend
Broadly sympathetic to environmental objections raised by activists

questions.explanation: B is correct because 'neither endorsing nor rejecting' and 'leaving bureaucrats free to interpret' both describe deliberate ambiguity — the hallmark of equivocal language. Option C is wrong because 'difficult to understand' confuses technical complexity with deliberate two-sidedness; equivocal is about double meaning, not jargon.

questions.stem: A passage reads: 'Classical dance forms like Manipuri and Kuchipudi receive a fraction of the funding directed at Bollywood, yet they carry centuries of narrative tradition and regional identity. One wonders whether our cultural policy truly reflects the diversity it claims to celebrate.' The author's PRIMARY purpose is to?

options.option_text: Provide a historical overview of Manipuri and Kuchipudi dance traditions
Question whether cultural funding priorities match India's stated diversity goals
Argue that Bollywood should be banned from receiving all government funding
Compare the commercial viability of classical versus popular entertainment forms

questions.explanation: B is correct because the rhetorical question 'One wonders whether our cultural policy truly reflects the diversity it claims to celebrate' is the argumentative core — the author is challenging policy consistency, not merely describing dance forms. Option C is wrong because the author never calls for a ban; the critique is about funding imbalance, not prohibition.

questions.stem: A researcher writes: 'Among the Santali people of Jharkhand, pera narratives encode collective migration memory and are now being reframed as secular folklore as younger generations urbanise. Seren, used exclusively in sacred ritual contexts, faces quiet extinction — unwitnessed by academia.' Which conclusion is BEST supported by the passage?

options.option_text: Literacy universally strengthens oral traditions by generating permanent written archives
Pera and seren face strictly identical threats from urbanisation and modernisation
Seren risks total extinction because its ritual-only context allows no secular adaptation
The researcher advocates that tribal communities should actively resist all urban migration

questions.explanation: C is correct through comparative reasoning: pera survives, transformed as secular folklore — a non-ritual second life. Seren, being exclusively ritual, has no such secular fallback pathway, making it uniquely vulnerable to total disappearance. Option B is wrong because the passage explicitly differentiates their fates: pera is 'reframed' (survives in altered form) while seren faces 'extinction' — identical threats would not produce different outcomes.

questions.stem: A passage reads: 'Critics who dismissed the novelist's early work as parochial now find themselves celebrating her Nobel recognition. Her prose, once condemned for its narrow regional focus, is now lauded as literary excavation — a recuperation of the suppressed vernacular against metropolitan aesthetics.' The word 'PAROCHIAL' as used here most accurately means?

options.option_text: Excessively spiritual and steeped in religious symbolism throughout the text
Needlessly lengthy and verbose, overwhelming readers with ornate stylistic excess
Dismissively viewed as too narrow or limited in geographic and cultural scope
Technically proficient in craft but lacking in emotional resonance for readers

questions.explanation: C is correct because the passage immediately glosses 'parochial' with 'narrow regional focus' — the critics condemned the work for being geographically/culturally restricted, which is the precise meaning of parochial. Option A is wrong because 'parochial' here is used in its literary-critical sense of narrow scope, not in its etymological ecclesiastical sense relating to a parish or religion.

questions.stem: Read the passage and answer: 'The ancient manuscripts stored in the libraries of Tanjore and Varanasi are deteriorating at an alarming rate. Inadequate storage facilities, humidity, and insect infestation are taking their toll on centuries of accumulated wisdom. If immediate steps are not taken, this irreplaceable cultural heritage will be lost forever.' The author's tone in this passage can best be described as which of the following?

options.option_text: casually indifferent to the deterioration problem
urgently concerned about the loss of cultural heritage
optimistically hopeful about imminent restoration efforts
academically detached and purely observational in stance

questions.explanation: B is correct because phrases like 'alarming rate', 'irreplaceable', and 'lost forever' signal urgency and deep concern, not detachment or optimism. Option C is wrong because the passage offers no hope of restoration — it warns of permanent loss if nothing is done, making optimism an inaccurate reading of the tone.

questions.stem: Read the passage and select the best title: 'Wetlands, often dismissed as wastelands, are among the most productive ecosystems on Earth. They filter pollutants from water, absorb floodwaters, and provide habitat for countless species. The Ramsar Convention recognises their global importance, yet India continues to lose wetlands to urban encroachment and agricultural conversion.' Which title best captures the central idea?

options.option_text: India's Urban Expansion and Its Environmental Consequences
Wetlands: Undervalued Ecosystems That Urgently Need Protection
The Ramsar Convention and Its Worldwide Conservation Role
Agricultural Conversion of Natural Habitats Across South Asia

questions.explanation: B is correct because the passage's core argument is that wetlands are wrongly dismissed despite their ecological value, and that India is still losing them — making protection the central theme. Option C is wrong because the Ramsar Convention is mentioned only in passing to support the main point; the passage is not about the Convention itself.

questions.stem: Read the passage and answer the inference question: 'The village of Pipli in Odisha has for centuries produced vibrant appliqué textiles — intricate patterns of cut and stitched coloured fabric. Today these products fetch premium prices in urban boutiques and are exported worldwide. Yet most artisans still earn below the minimum wage, as middlemen capture the bulk of the value chain.' What can be most logically inferred from this passage?

options.option_text: Pipli appliqué craft products find no real market outside Odisha
Artisans fully benefit from the rising global demand for their craft
Market success of a craft need not translate to artisan prosperity
Odisha has formally banned middlemen from the craft supply chain

questions.explanation: C is correct because the passage explicitly shows a contradiction: the craft commands premium prices globally, yet the makers earn below minimum wage — the surplus flows to middlemen, not artisans. Option B directly contradicts the passage's stated fact. Option D is unsupported; the passage describes the problem of middlemen but makes no claim about government action.

questions.stem: Read the sentence and answer: 'The committee's report was deliberately EQUIVOCAL — neither endorsing nor rejecting the proposed policy — leaving administrators in a state of uncertainty about the intended direction.' In this context, EQUIVOCAL most nearly means which of the following?

options.option_text: deliberately ambiguous and non-committal in its overall stance
strongly supportive of the proposed administrative measures
excessively technical and therefore difficult to comprehend
visibly biased in favour of one side of the argument only

questions.explanation: A is correct because the passage itself defines the word's meaning — the report endorsed nothing and rejected nothing, causing uncertainty — which is precisely what 'equivocal' (ambiguous, open to two interpretations) means. Option C is tempting because complex reports can be hard to understand, but difficulty of comprehension is not what the passage describes; it describes deliberate fence-sitting.

questions.stem: Read the passage and identify the author's primary purpose: 'Despite winning two Grand Slam titles, Leander Paes remains largely unknown among India's urban youth, who reserve their admiration exclusively for cricketers. The invisibility of non-cricket sports in media coverage perpetuates a cycle where sponsors follow eyeballs, not excellence, consigning gifted athletes to obscurity and penury.' The primary purpose of this passage is to do which of the following?

options.option_text: celebrate Leander Paes's specific Grand Slam career in detail
argue that cricket must receive reduced media broadcast funding
show how media bias systematically marginalises non-cricket athletes
compare the commercial sponsorship value of cricket versus tennis

questions.explanation: C is correct because Paes is used as an illustrative example, not the subject; the passage's logical thrust is that a structural media-sponsor feedback loop disadvantages all non-cricket sports. Option A is wrong because the passage does not detail Paes's career — it merely references him to make a broader systemic point. Option D is wrong because the comparison is incidental, not the author's purpose.

questions.stem: Read the passage carefully and identify the author's stance: 'The discourse on artificial intelligence in Indian governance oscillates between utopian enthusiasm and dystopian anxiety, rarely pausing at the pragmatic middle ground. Proponents tout AI as a panacea for corruption and inefficiency; critics warn of algorithmic bias amplifying existing inequities. What is conspicuously absent from both camps is empirical data drawn from actual Indian administrative contexts.' Which of the following best describes the author's position?

options.option_text: enthusiastically supportive of rapid AI adoption across governance
primarily critical of AI's potential to deepen social inequalities
sceptical of both extremes and calling for evidence-based policy discourse
dismissive of AI as broadly irrelevant to India's governance challenges

questions.explanation: C is correct because the author critiques both the proponents (utopian panacea claim) and the critics (dystopian warnings) with equal distance, and the final sentence pinpoints that what both sides lack is empirical data — a call for evidence-based pragmatism. Option B is tempting because the passage does mention algorithmic bias, but the author does not endorse the critics' position; the author equally distances from them, making B a partial misreading.

questions.stem: Read the passage and answer: 'When the Lokpal Bill finally passed after decades of public agitation, civil society celebrated it as a landmark victory. Three years later, the institution remained without a chairperson for extended periods, its investigative powers constrained by procedural hurdles, and whistleblower complaints accumulated without adjudication. The celebration, it seems, was for the letter of the law, not its spirit.' The final sentence implies which of the following most precisely?

options.option_text: the Act was deliberately drafted with loopholes to legally curb its reach
civil society wrongly celebrated legislation that was never formally enacted
the law exists formally on paper but lacks the operational will to deliver
celebrating any legislation is premature until superior courts formally validate it

questions.explanation: C is correct because 'letter of the law' means the formal text exists, while 'spirit of the law' means its intended purpose — justice and accountability. The passage shows the law was passed but is operationally hollow (no chairperson, blocked powers, unresolved complaints), confirming a gap between legal form and functional reality. Option A is a plausible trap because intent could be inferred, but the passage does not claim deliberate sabotage — only operational failure. Option D introduces a judicial validation angle that the passage never mentions.
